children.text: When it comes to motion recognition, I'm referring to video clips where you can still make out what's happening—for example, reaching out to pick up an apple. Even though there are a few frames of motion blur in between, you can still clearly see that the apple was picked up.

source.text: While filtering a video dataset for training, I noticed that using a blur filter not only removes out-of-focus clips but also some motion-blurred clips that contain useful information. Aside from limited manual review, how do you identify useful clips from those automatically filtered out?
source.title: Ask HN: How do you identify video samples that were mistakenly deleted?
